conviction_note: Nothing decisive and unpriced turned up. The small positives are a Q3 bitcoin mark-to-market gain (~$16M, ~$0.12/unit), oil rising through the quarter, the AllDale III & IV consolidation and Hamilton's return to longwall. All but the bitcoin gain sit inside the July guide. Against them, broad US coal output and demand series are soft and S&P flagged price pressure for new contracts. p_up 55 times abs 4.0 gives +0.4; the findings sum to +0.25, and the two agree in sign and order of size.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS $0.82 (3 analysts, AAII 2026-10-23 https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/520342-what-you-need-to-know-about-alliance-resource-partners-lps-q3-earnings; Benzinga $0.82) to $0.84 (Earnings Whispers), revenue $588.8-590.0M (Benzinga / Earnings Whispers via search). Company FY2026 guide (8-K 2026-07-27 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001086600/000110465926086855/arlp-20260727xex99d1.htm): coal sales 33.75-35.25M tons, price $54-56/t, cost $37-39/t. H1 sold 16.42M tons, so the midpoint implies ~9.0M tons a quarter in H2 against 8.56M in Q2. The two estimate sources agree within $0.02, so the bar is usable. My revenue read: ~9.0M t x ~$55 coal plus a larger consolidated royalty line comes to about $595-600M, roughly 1% above the bar.
positioning_check: Short interest 1.6M units at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, 6.3 days to cover (1.4M at 09-15), via Curved Trading (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/arlp/short-interest/). That is about 1.2% of the 128.66M units outstanding (10-Q cover), so not a crowded short. Skew is null in the baseline. Put/call open interest is 0.21 (call-heavy) on only 2,000 contracts total. The ATM spread is 60% of mid, so the 5.97% implied move is indicative only. 20-day realised vol is 15.3% annualised; the stock is +3.86% over 20 days and 9.9% below its 52-week high. No directional statement from options.

findings.finding: Q3 should carry a bitcoin fair-value gain, which consensus EPS likely does not model. ARLP held 646 BTC worth $37.9M at 2026-06-30 (~$58.7k each). Bitcoin closed Q3 2026 up 42.71%, which implies ~$54M at 9/30 and a ~$16M non-operating gain (~$0.12/unit on 128.66M units). Q2 had a $6.3M loss. Against $0.82-0.84 consensus, this alone could put GAAP EPS around $0.95. EBITDA and DCF exclude it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2025 carried a $12.9M BTC gain (per the Q2 2026 release comparison) and the stock fell 1.72% on that print (2025-07-28). The market has not rewarded BTC marks.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side Q3 EPS ($0.82-0.85) is a step-up of ~$0.20 from Q2's $0.61. That is consistent with volume and royalty recovery and no BTC mark, but the analysts' inclusion of a mark is not verifiable. If the market priced it as earnings, the headline 'beat' would already be expected. Below operating income, so its weight in the reaction is small.
findings.independence: BTC Q3 return from a different source: https://pro.edgex.exchange/en-US/news/article/bitcoin-q3-2026-best-quarter-since-2017 (2026-10-01). The holding count and price come from the company 8-K. Unknown: whether ARLP sold any BTC in Q3.

findings.finding: The oil & gas royalty segment, a record $38.0M segment EBITDA in Q2, gets two lifts in Q3. First, Brent rose through the quarter: ~$72 on July 1, above $100 on July 23, $79-98 to September 8, then a ~$104 average over the last two weeks of September. Second, the $206.2M AllDale III & IV acquisition (48,500 net royalty acres) closed July 1, and AllDale III is consolidated from Q3. Q2's average oil price is not sourced, and Henry Hub ran ~$2.9 in Q3, so the realized $/BOE change from Q2's $49.43 is uncertain. The acquisition volumes are already in the raised royalty guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 posted record royalty revenue (+30.5% YoY) and the stock rose 3.72% on 2026-07-27, though on a mixed EPS read.
findings.why_not_priced: The acquisition volume is in guidance and therefore priced. The late-quarter oil spike may not be in three-analyst models updated in late July (Noble, Sidoti). If it were priced, revisions over the last month would be up. AAII shows one upgrade and no downgrades in the month to 2026-10-23, so it is partly priced at most.
findings.independence: EIA October STEO overview puts Brent at $96 for 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/archives/oct26.pdf). The acquisition and consolidation come from the company's 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1086600/000110465926092001/arlp-20260630x10q.htm).

findings.finding: Hamilton (Illinois Basin) is back on longwall after an extended Q2 move, and management says no further longwall moves until 2027. Hitting the 2026 guide midpoint needs ~9.0M tons a quarter in H2 against 8.56M in Q2, with 34.3M of 2026 tons committed and priced (fully contracted at midpoint). This lands inside guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume recoveries are usually pre-signalled by this company; the last four prints rose 2.2-4.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: management said it, and consensus revenue of $590M (vs $552M in Q2) already embeds the H2 volume step-up.
findings.independence: Call recap: Hamilton could add 1.0-1.3M tons in 2027 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/alliance-resource-partners-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-27/). Same company source.

findings.finding: Broad US coal output was soft in Q3. EIA weekly data show US mines produced 4.1% less than a year earlier over the 10 weeks to September 5. Argus says utilities stayed out of the spot market on adequate inventory and low gas prices. Weekly Illinois output for the week to August 29 was down 8.5% YoY. EIA's Q3 production forecast is 130.9M st vs 135.9M a year earlier. This is a deferral risk to ARLP's H2 shipments even with a contracted book.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2025 (-1.72%) and Q4 2024 (2025-02-03, -3.83%) were the down prints in the baseline. The cause of those moves was not established here.
findings.why_not_priced: The series is public and broad, so it is likely priced into the sector. ARLP's 2026 book is fully committed and the company said weak H1 demand had minimal impact. If the market feared deferrals, the stock would not be within 10% of its high with call-heavy open interest. This is a proxy, not a company number.
findings.independence: Illinois weekly figure via https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/?p=888461 (EIA data). It is the same EIA dataset, so not independent of the Argus piece.

findings.finding: Power-sector coal stockpiles fell to an estimated 100M short tons at end-September 2026, from 105M a year earlier (EIA STEO of 2026-10-06). EIA says the sector drew stocks to meet high summer electricity demand. That supports Q3 contracted shipments taken in full and utility appetite for 2027 contracting. It partly offsets the production-weakness series above.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 print (2025-10-27) +4.12%. The relevance of 2027 contracting updates to that move is not sourced.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public EIA number, so mostly priced. It matters only to the extent the release shows new 2027 commitments above the 29.4M tons committed in July. This is a proxy.
findings.independence: It contrasts with the Argus/S&P inventory-overhang narrative (https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/2026/07/slack-demand-surging-inventory-pressurize-us-coal-prices). Different sources point opposite ways.

findings.finding: The forward demand and price backdrop for new 2027 contracts is weak, and Q3 releases typically update 2027 committed and priced tons (29.4M in July). S&P Global (July 2026) says slack demand and surging inventory pressure US coal prices. EIA's October STEO projects US coal consumption falling from 424M st in 2026 to 405M in 2027 and lower coal generation this winter on low gas and retirements. New 2027 tonnage may be priced below 2026's $54-56/t.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2025's pricing step-down coincided with -1.72%. Q2 2026's Appalachia price fell to $63.57 from $74.51 and the stock still rose 3.72%. Mixed.
findings.why_not_priced: The sector-wide outlook is public. What is not public is ARLP's 2027 price on new commitments. If the market expected 2027 pricing well below 2026, the stock would trade lower than 9.9% off its high with a 1.39x-covered 9.2% yield. A proxy, sized small.
findings.independence: S&P Global July 2026 headline (https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/2026/07/slack-demand-surging-inventory-pressurize-us-coal-prices), a different source from EIA.

findings.finding: The distribution is likely held at $0.60/unit ($2.40 annualised). Q2 coverage was 1.39x on $108.2M DCF, but July's $206.2M acquisition was funded with cash, revolver borrowings and a new $150M minerals term loan maturing January 2028, and management emphasised leverage reduction. A raise is possible on coverage but not signalled. A hold is the expectation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $0.60 distribution has been held since the 2025 cut; the prints that held it (2025-07 through 2026-07) ranged -1.72% to +4.12%.
findings.why_not_priced: A hold is priced. A raise would be the surprise and nothing points to one.
findings.independence: Q2 release coverage figures: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001086600/000110465926086855/arlp-20260727xex99d1.htm. Leverage focus: https://quartr.com/events/alliance-resource-partners-lp-arlp-q2-2026_ozmz0e5W.

findings.finding: The 10-Q says ARLP will remeasure its previously held AllDale III equity-method investment (carrying value $20.1M at 6/30) at fair value immediately before the July 1 acquisition, using a DCF. That produces a Q3 gain or loss of unknown size. With oil prices elevated at the deal date, a gain is somewhat more likely. Below operating income.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a footnote item no estimate models. It is also a non-cash one-off with no path to DCF or guidance, so it is worth little.
findings.independence: None. Related: Craft-related entities acquired $100M of AllDale III LP interests (same 10-Q), and ARLP consolidates with ~53% noncontrolling interest.

findings.finding: Insider activity since the last print is trivial. An officer, Mark Watson, filed a Form 144 on 2026-09-15 to sell 6,606 units (~$172.7k) acquired as equity compensation. Director Ronna McDaniel bought 69.74 units at $25.81 on 2026-08-18 (~$1.8k). There is no cluster.
findings.why_not_priced: Too small to matter. It is filed for completeness.
